items.name: Haldi (Turmeric) Powder
items.why: Used for Ganapati puja at the start. Turmeric represents purity and is essential for making the Ganapati idol from turmeric paste.

items.name: Kumkum (Vermillion)
items.why: Applied to the deity as a mark of auspiciousness. Represents Goddess Lakshmi's blessings.

items.name: Chandan (Sandalwood) Paste
items.why: Applied to deity and devotees. Its cooling property symbolizes the calming presence of Lord Vishnu.

items.name: Akshata (Turmeric Rice)
items.why: Unbroken turmeric-coated rice offered to the deity. Represents prosperity and completeness.

items.name: Coconut
items.why: Offered to Lord Vishnu. The three eyes of coconut represent the three eyes of Lord Shiva. Breaking it symbolizes breaking the ego.

items.name: Banana
items.why: Pure satvik fruit offered as naivedyam. Banana is considered the most sacred fruit in Hindu worship.

items.name: Betel Leaves (Tambulam)
items.why: Used in puja offerings and given as prasadam. Represents respect and is part of the 16 upacharas.

items.name: Betel Nuts (Supari)
items.why: Paired with betel leaves in offerings. Symbolizes the seed of creation.

items.name: Incense Sticks
items.why: Dhoop offering purifies the atmosphere and represents the element of air (Vayu).

items.name: Camphor
items.why: For aarti. Camphor burns completely leaving no residue — symbolizing the dissolution of ego before God.

items.name: Cotton Wicks
items.why: For lighting diyas. The flame represents knowledge dispelling darkness of ignorance.

items.name: Ghee
items.why: For diya and naivedyam. Pure cow ghee is the most satvik fuel for the sacred flame.

items.name: Puja Vidhi Booklet
items.why: Step-by-step puja instructions in your chosen regional language with Sanskrit mantras and their meaning.

items.name: Vrat Katha Book
items.why: The five sacred stories of Lord Satyanarayan that are read aloud during the puja. Reading the katha is an essential part of the vratam.

additionalItems.name: Yellow Thread (Mauli)
additionalItems.why: Tied as protection thread after puja. Yellow is Lord Vishnu's color representing preservation.

additionalItems.name: Panchamrit Ingredients
additionalItems.why: Milk, curd, honey, sugar, ghee — the five sacred nectars for deity abhishekam, representing the five elements.

additionalItems.name: Mango Leaves
additionalItems.why: Placed in the kalash (sacred pot). Mango leaves represent the wish-fulfilling tree and invite positive energy.

additionalItems.name: Yellow Cloth (Vastram)
additionalItems.why: Deity clothing. Yellow represents knowledge and is Lord Vishnu's sacred color (Pitambara).

additionalItems.name: 5 Varieties of Fruits
additionalItems.why: Offered as naivedyam. Five fruits represent the five elements and five senses being offered to God.

additionalItems.name: Sheera/Prasad Ingredients
additionalItems.why: For preparing the traditional naivedyam (semolina halwa). This prasadam is distributed to all present after the katha.

additionalItems.name: Puja Kalash (Brass)
additionalItems.why: The sacred pot filled with water, topped with coconut — represents the universe and is the seat of Lord Vishnu during the puja.

additionalItems.name: Rangoli/Muggulu Powder
additionalItems.why: For decorating the puja area. Traditional floor art invites Goddess Lakshmi into the home.

additionalItems.name: Premium Brass Puja Set
additionalItems.why: Complete brass puja items (thali, bell, diya, spoon) for an authentic traditional experience.

additionalItems.name: Silver Coin (Lakshmi-Narayan)
additionalItems.why: Placed in the kalash. Silver represents the moon's energy and Lakshmi's blessings.

additionalItems.name: Fresh Flower Garlands
additionalItems.why: For deity decoration. Fresh flowers represent the devotee's pure heart offered to God.

additionalItems.name: Havan Samagri
additionalItems.why: Sacred herbs for the fire ritual. The 21+ herbs purify the atmosphere and carry prayers to the heavens.

additionalItems.name: Premium Prasadam Box
additionalItems.why: For distributing blessed prasadam to neighbors and relatives — sharing divine blessings.

items.name: Eco-Friendly Ganesh Murti
items.why: Clay idol of Lord Ganesha. Eco-friendly ensures the idol dissolves naturally during visarjan without harming the environment.

items.name: Durva Grass
items.why: Durva (Bermuda grass) is Lord Ganesha's most beloved offering. The 21 blades represent the 21 'offerings of the self.'

items.name: 21 Types of Patra (Leaves)
items.why: Traditional offering of 21 different sacred leaves, each representing a different aspect of nature's bounty offered to Ganapati.

items.name: Modak Ingredients
items.why: Modak is Lord Ganesha's favorite sweet. Making modak at home is part of the devotional tradition.

items.name: Red Flowers
items.why: Red is Lord Ganesha's favorite color. Red hibiscus (japa pushpa) is especially dear to him.

items.name: Kumkum & Turmeric
items.why: Essential puja materials. Kumkum represents the third eye of wisdom, turmeric represents purity.

items.name: Coconut
items.why: Offered during puja and broken during visarjan as a symbol of surrendering the ego.

items.name: Incense & Camphor
items.why: For daily aarti during the festival. Morning and evening aarti is essential during Ganesh Chaturthi.
